title: An Integrated Brain-Machine Interface Platform With Thousands of Channels
why: Neuralink describes flexible electrode threads, insertion robotics and recording hardware.
caution: The 2019 platform paper is not evidence of human mind uploading or current clinical efficacy.

title: High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting
authors: Willett FR, Avansino DT, Hochberg LR, Henderson JM, Shenoy KV.
why: Decodes attempted handwriting into text in a participant with paralysis.
caution: Single-participant demonstration; not general thought reading.

title: A high-performance speech neuroprosthesis
authors: Willett FR, Kunz EM, Fan C, Avansino DT, Wilson GH, Choi EY, Kamdar F, Glasser MF, Hochberg LR, Druckmann S, Shenoy KV, Henderson JM.
why: Decodes attempted speech into text using intracortical arrays.
caution: One participant; accuracy depends strongly on vocabulary and task.

title: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control
authors: Metzger SL, Littlejohn KT, Silva AB, Moses DA, Seaton MP, Wang R, Dougherty ME, Liu JR, Wu P, Berger MA, Zhuravleva I, Tu-Chan A, Ganguly K, Anumanchipalli GK, Chang EF.
why: Combines decoded speech text, synthesized audio and facial-avatar control.
caution: One clinical-trial participant; trained task-specific decoding.

title: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis
authors: Card NS, Wairagkar M, Iacobacci C, Hou X, Singer-Clark T, Willett FR, Kunz EM, Fan C, Vahdati Nia M, Deo DR, Srinivasan A, Choi EY, Glasser MF, Hochberg LR, Henderson JM, Shahlaie K, Stavisky SD, Brandman DM.
venue: The New England journal of medicine
why: Demonstrates a rapidly calibrated speech prosthesis used in conversation.
caution: One person with ALS; longer-term general use and broader populations need testing.

title: A streaming brain-to-voice neuroprosthesis to restore naturalistic communication
authors: Littlejohn KT, Cho CJ, Liu JR, Silva AB, Yu B, Anderson VR, Kurtz-Miott CM, Brosler S, Kashyap AP, Hallinan IP, Shah A, Tu-Chan A, Ganguly K, Moses DA, Chang EF, Anumanchipalli GK.
why: Streams synthesized speech from cortical recordings in short increments.
caution: Early clinical demonstration, not unrestricted access to private thoughts.

title: A high-performance brain-computer interface for finger decoding and quadcopter game control in an individual with paralysis
authors: Willsey MS, Shah NP, Avansino DT, Hahn NV, Jamiolkowski RM, Kamdar FB, Hochberg LR, Willett FR, Henderson JM.
why: Decodes finger movements for virtual quadcopter game control.
caution: One participant and a virtual task, not flight-safety evidence.

title: High performance communication by people with paralysis using an intracortical brain-computer interface
authors: Pandarinath C, Nuyujukian P, Blabe CH, Sorice BL, Saab J, Willett FR, Hochberg LR, Shenoy KV, Henderson JM.
why: Tests higher-performance intracortical communication in three people with paralysis.
caution: Small clinical study; performance is not a universal user outcome.

title: Semantic reconstruction of continuous language from non-invasive brain recordings
authors: Tang J, LeBel A, Jain S, Huth AG.
why: Reconstructs the meaning of language from non-invasive fMRI signals.
caution: Cooperation and extensive subject-specific training matter; not a portable mind reader.

title: Towards decoding individual words from non-invasive brain recordings
authors: d'Ascoli S, Bel C, Rapin J, Banville H, Benchetrit Y, Pallier C, King JR.
why: Benchmarks word decoding from EEG and MEG across multiple datasets.
caution: Stimulus/task and recording-device dependent; not evidence of arbitrary private-thought decoding.

title: A brain-spine interface alleviating gait deficits after spinal cord injury in primates
authors: Capogrosso M, Milekovic T, Borton D, Wagner F, Moraud EM, Mignardot JB, Buse N, Gandar J, Barraud Q, Xing D, Rey E, Rey E, Duis S, Jianzhong Y, Ko WK, Li Q, Detemple P, Denison T, Micera S, Bezard E, Bloch J, Courtine G.
why: Links brain signals to spinal stimulation to improve locomotion in injured primates.
caution: Non-human primate proof of concept; separate from the later human study.

title: Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface
authors: Lorach H, Galvez A, Spagnolo V, Martel F, Karakas S, Intering N, Vat M, Faivre O, Harte C, Komi S, Ravier J, Collin T, Coquoz L, Sakr I, Baaklini E, Hernandez-Charpak SD, Dumont G, Buschman R, Buse N, Denison T, van Nes I, Asboth L, Watrin A, Struber L, Sauter-Starace F, Langar L, Auboiroux V, Carda S, Chabardes S, Aksenova T, Demesmaeker R, Charvet G, Bloch J, Courtine G.
why: A brain-spine digital bridge supports walking after chronic spinal cord injury.
caution: An individual clinical demonstration, not a general cure for paralysis.

title: Restoration of reaching and grasping movements through brain-controlled muscle stimulation in a person with tetraplegia: a proof-of-concept demonstration
authors: Ajiboye AB, Willett FR, Young DR, Memberg WD, Murphy BA, Miller JP, Walter BL, Sweet JA, Hoyen HA, Keith MW, Peckham PH, Simeral JD, Donoghue JP, Hochberg LR, Kirsch RF.
why: Brain-controlled muscle stimulation restores reaching and grasping in one participant.
caution: Proof of concept with implanted electrodes and assistive support.

title: A wireless millimetric magnetoelectric implant for the endovascular stimulation of peripheral nerves
authors: Chen JC, Kan P, Yu Z, Alrashdan F, Garcia R, Singer A, Lai CSE, Avants B, Crosby S, Li Z, Wang B, Felicella MM, Robledo A, Peterchev AV, Goetz SM, Hartgerink JD, Sheth SA, Yang K, Robinson JT.
why: Tests a small wireless endovascular peripheral-nerve stimulation implant.
caution: Adjacent neurotechnology, not a cortical BCI; tested in rats and pigs.

title: Fully Implanted Brain-Computer Interface in a Locked-In Patient with ALS
authors: Vansteensel MJ, Pels EGM, Bleichner MG, Branco MP, Denison T, Freudenburg ZV, Gosselaar P, Leinders S, Ottens TH, Van Den Boom MA, Van Rijen PC, Aarnoutse EJ, Ramsey NF.
venue: The New England journal of medicine
why: A fully implanted BCI supports typing in a locked-in person with ALS.
caution: One participant; slow communication, not speech restoration or uploading.

title: Neuroprosthesis for Decoding Speech in a Paralyzed Person with Anarthria
authors: Moses DA, Metzger SL, Liu JR, Anumanchipalli GK, Makin JG, Sun PF, Chartier J, Dougherty ME, Liu PM, Abrams GM, Tu-Chan A, Ganguly K, Chang EF.
venue: The New England journal of medicine
why: Decodes attempted words and sentences in a person with anarthria.
caution: One participant and a constrained vocabulary; not silent omniscient mind reading.

title: High-performance neuroprosthetic control by an individual with tetraplegia
authors: Collinger JL, Wodlinger B, Downey JE, Wang W, Tyler-Kabara EC, Weber DJ, McMorland AJ, Velliste M, Boninger ML, Schwartz AB.
why: Demonstrates multi-degree-of-freedom robotic-arm control after tetraplegia.
caution: Individual proof of concept requiring surgical implants and training.

title: Assessment of Safety of a Fully Implanted Endovascular Brain-Computer Interface for Severe Paralysis in 4 Patients: The Stentrode With Thought-Controlled Digital Switch (SWITCH) Study
authors: Mitchell P, Lee SCM, Yoo PE, Morokoff A, Sharma RP, Williams DL, MacIsaac C, Howard ME, Irving L, Vrljic I, Williams C, Bush S, Balabanski AH, Drummond KJ, Desmond P, Weber D, Denison T, Mathers S, O'Brien TJ, Mocco J, Grayden DB, Liebeskind DS, Opie NL, Oxley TJ, Campbell BCV.
why: The SWITCH study assesses an endovascular BCI and computer control.
caution: Four analyzed patients and 12-month follow-up cannot establish rare-event or population-wide safety.
